name: 5-inch High Velocity Aircraft Rocket (HVAR)
blurb: The rocket on every strike loadout's rails. Its model is generated from the Smithsonian's measured example and the Navy's ordnance pamphlet.
history:
The HVAR, nicknamed Holy Moses, was a 5-inch unguided rocket developed at the California Institute of Technology for the Navy and first fired in 1944. A 5-inch motor gave it a much higher velocity than the earlier forward-firing rockets, so it flew flatter and hit harder, and it could pierce armor and concrete.

Fighters carried it on zero-length launchers under the wings, in pairs, and it saw heavy use against ships, bunkers and armor in the Pacific and in Europe. More than a million were built, and it stayed in service into the Korean War.
